capabilities: Create cards from the active note with trace links back to the source
Parse Markdown into Q&A, cloze, fill-in and multiple-choice cards
Schedule reviews with FSRS6 across formal and reference-based decks
Jump from a card to its source passage, block reference, Canvas node or EPUB location
Import and export APKG, CSV and vault backups
disambiguation: Not a proofreading or note-review tool; "review" here means spaced-repetition study of flashcards.
extras: Freemium: the core FSRS/Markdown/parse-preview/retention/API/APKG loop is free, while advanced analytics, management views, emergent decks, exam banks and AI need a buy-once Premium activation; some features offer limited-time trials. Cards and decks live in .wdeck/.qbank files that should not be hand-edited or bulk-renamed; third-party plugins should write through getOfficialAPI().
intentEvidence: You write in Markdown; the plugin parses and previews that structure as question types—instead of Anki-style field forms.
problem: Flashcards made in Obsidian usually drift away from the notes they came from, so reviewing loses the original context and the card has to be maintained as a separate form.

relations.evidence: EPUB Reader adds in-book excerpts and book-anchor jumps
Incremental Reading handles reading queues and scheduling
Community tools such as PDF++, Excalidraw, Media Extended, Mind Map, etc.

summary: Spaced-repetition flashcard plugin that turns Markdown notes into source-linked cards, reviews them with FSRS6, and jumps back to the original passage.
